items.title: Supreme Court seeks data on life insurance policies issued to persons with autism, cerebral palsy
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday asked the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) to place on record data on the number of life insurance policies issued to persons with autism, cerebral palsy and Asperger’s syndrome [ Action for Autism vs. Union of India ]. A Bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice R Mahadevan passed the direction while hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by the Non-Governmental Organisation (NGO) Action for Autism. Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice R Mahadevan The plea seeks systemic reforms to protect and promote the rights of persons with neurodivergent conditions such as autism, dyslexia and Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). During the hearing today, counsel appearing for the IRDAI told the Court that two circulars had already been issued concerning the provision of insurance to persons with autism. The circulars had also been placed on record along with IRDAI’s counter-affidavit. The Court, however, sought to know whether life insurance policies had actually been issued to persons with autism. items.summary: A public interest litigation (PIL) petition has been filed before the Delhi High Court challenging the requirement of three years’ practice at the Bar for direct recruitment to the post of Assistant Public Prosecutor (APP) in the Delhi Directorate of Prosecution. items.title: BCI can promote legal education but can it control law colleges? Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday questioned the extent to which the Bar Council of India (BCI) can interfere in matters of legal education [ Girish Mittal v. Bar Council of India and ors ]. The Court orally observed that the BCI cannot control the running of law colleges, even though it has a role in regulating law college curriculum, the period of study and the general promotion of legal education. “ You can lay down the curriculum, whether it should be four years, five years. You can promote legal education and for that, you can take promotional measures. But you can't control it. What do you know about legal education? There are experts ,” remarked Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. The Bench of CJI Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing a plea related to the use of funds transferred to the BCI Trust PEARL-First, which in 2020 replaced the erstwhile BCI trust that had been in place since 1974. CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, Justice V Mohana In particular, the petitioner, Girish Mittal, has raised questions about the creation and functioning of two law colleges in Goa and Andhra Pradesh. The Court found serious lapses in the investigations conducted by the local police, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI). The possibility of the real culprit(s) manipulating the investigation cannot be ruled out. Such lax and improper investigation gives premium to the Investigating Officers who failed to do their job correctly and diligently, ” the Court said. items.title: Kerala High Court grants bail to school teacher arrested in Vadakara drug trafficking case
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday granted bail to a school teacher arrested in connection with a drug trafficking case registered by the Vadakara police [Kavya K v State of Kerala]. Justice Kauser Edappagath allowed the bail application of 29-year-old Kavya K, who is the third accused in the case. While granting bail, the Court took into account Kavya's judicial custody since July 25. " The applicant was remanded to judicial custody on 25.07.2026. The investigation is almost over. The recovery has been effected. The applicant has no criminal antecedents. For these reasons, I do not find any reason to hold that the continued detention of the applicant is required for any purpose. Hence, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail, " the Court said. Justice Kauser Edappagath The bail plea was filed in connection with the crime registered by the Vadakara Police. Kavya was booked under Section 22(b) and Section 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 (NDPS Act), for offences relating to possession of psychotropic substances and criminal conspiracy. items.title: DHCBA objects to Central Motor Vehicles Rules amendments on traffic challans
items.summary: The Delhi High Court Bar Association (DHCBA) has voiced deep concern and strong objection to the recent amendments made to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 governing the adjudication of traffic challans. In a resolution passed on Wednesday, association's executive committee called on the concerned authorities to reconsider the changes, emphasising that disputed traffic challans must remain subject to effective, independent and accessible judicial scrutiny. Therefore, the bar body objected to the changes as per which contested challans are now required to be initially adjudicated by executive or departmental authorities rather than an independent judicial forum. "Disputed questions concerning the facts, evidence and liability arising from a challan ought to be adjudicated by an independent judicial forum only," the resolution stated. The DHCBA further flagged the requirement mandating a pre-deposit of 50 percent of the challan amount before approaching a competent court. This is a substantial financial impediment that curbs access to judicial remedies, particularly for ordinary citizens, the DHCBA said. Meanwhile, the Court also observed that Nair cannot challenge the non-bailable warrant when it already stands executed. items.title: Delhi High Court directs police inquiry into fabrication of court order
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently directed the Commissioner of Police to inquire into the alleged fabrication of a 2024 court order on finding that an additional paragraph stating “interim stay granted” - which the Court had not added - was found in a version of its order [ Meena Devi & Anr. v The State & Ors. ]. Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav found that the original order passed on November 19, 2024 contained only three paragraphs. It had merely adjourned the matter till January 14, 2025, while directing that a trial court record be requisitioned. However, a version of the same order produced before the Court contained an additional fourth paragraph stating, “Interim stay granted.” While examining the discrepancy, the Court in its September 18 order held, "Some unknown person seems to have fabricated the order passed by this Court and added para. 4 containing the words 'interim stay granted'. The said aspect requires to be investigated and appropriate action has to be taken." items.title: NSE phone tapping case: Delhi High Court rejects CBI challenge to Chitra Ramkrishna's bail
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday rejected the plea filed by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) challenging the trial court order granting bail to former NSE managing director Chitra Ramkrishna in the alleged NSE phone tapping case. Justice Madhu Jain passed the order. Justice Madhu Jain The case relates to alleged illegal interceptions of phone calls of NSE employees between 2009 and 2017. According to the CBI, Ramkrishna, along with former CEO Ravi Narain, Executive Vice-President Ravi Varanasi and Head (Premises) Mahesh Haldipur, allegedly engaged iSEC Services to intercept NSE employees' calls under the guise of conducting a periodic study of cyber vulnerabilities at the exchange. The trial court granted Ramkrishna bail in December 2022, prompting the CBI to move the High Court.
